Flow chart of company formation in Nigeria. Four connected boxes pointing right. Box 1: "Promoters prepare Memorandum & Articles of Association". Box 2: "Filing documents and paying fees at the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC)". Box 3: "CAC reviews and approves". Box 4: "CAC issues Certificate of Incorporation". Clean flat textbook illustration, white background, corporate blue and green colours.

Block diagram representing the financing of a company. A large vertical rectangle is split into two halves. The left half is "Total Assets" consisting of a top block "Non-Current Assets" and a bottom block "Current Assets". The right half shows how it is funded: top block "Equity (Share Capital + Reserves)", middle block "Non-Current Liabilities (Debentures)", bottom block "Current Liabilities". Arrows show that both sides must equal the same total value.

Visual analogy of Liquidity Ratios. Two sets of weighing scales. Scale 1 (Current Ratio): Left pan holds "Current Assets" (shown as icons of cash, bank, debtors, and boxes of stock), right pan holds "Current Liabilities" (bills and invoices). Scale 2 (Acid Test Ratio): Left pan holds only cash, bank, and debtors (the boxes of stock are crossed out with a red X), right pan holds the same "Current Liabilities". This shows stock is removed from the quick assets.
